operations_plan.summary: Shorten the long high-reach Nozzle Volcano by exactly 1 mm at the free end of its externally threaded shank, while preserving the hex drive, conical tip, outlet, thread specification, and nozzle axis.

steps.description: Isolate solid 8 in section_8 as the Nozzle Volcano. Establish the nozzle center axis from the coaxial cylindrical external-thread and internal-bore faces. Identify the threaded shank's free terminal end opposite the hexagonal drive. The exact terminal face is not individually resolved in the supplied face ranges, so select it by topology as the planar annular end face bounding the upper end of the long external thread and internal passage. Confirm that the axial distance to be changed lies entirely within the threaded area above the hexagonal seating shoulder.

Create a datum plane normal to the nozzle center axis and parallel to the existing free terminal face. Offset this plane exactly 1.0 mm from the existing terminal face toward the hexagonal drive and seating shoulder. Use the existing free-end face and the axis established in the preceding step as references; do not reference or move the hexagonal drive or nozzle tip.

Shorten the threaded shank to the offset datum plane. Prefer editing the parent shank-length or thread-length parameter so the free-end boundary moves 1.0 mm toward the hex; if no editable parent feature exists, remove the 1.0 mm axial slab between the original terminal face and the offset plane with a planar cut normal to the nozzle axis. Apply the cut only to solid 8. The cut must trim both the external threaded envelope and the coaxial internal passage at the free end, producing a new planar annular terminal face while leaving the bore diameter and all geometry below the datum plane unchanged.

Regenerate or trim the detailed external thread against the new terminal boundary. Preserve the existing major diameter, minor diameter, pitch, flank profile, handedness, helix axis, and coaxial alignment. Relocate the original free-end thread lead-in, chamfer, and runout to the new terminal end when those features exist; retain their original dimensions and keep them inside the shortened envelope. Do not alter the thread-to-hex runout or seating shoulder. The resulting usable threaded engagement length is exactly 1.0 mm shorter.

Recompute solid 8 and verify that its overall axial height is exactly 1.0 mm less than the original measurement. Confirm that the hexagonal drive and seating shoulder, conical tip, outlet orifice, and their relative axial positions are unchanged. Verify continuity and concentricity of the internal flow passage, valid thread geometry at the new end, and absence of self-intersections or residual thread fragments. Confirm that solids 0 through 7 and all other assembly sections remain unmodified.
